title: Oven Preheat Readiness Confirmation
dataSources: Sourdough monitor (`sourdough:reading`), BBQ/sous-vide probes (`bbq:probe`), fridge/freezer/oven temperature (`kitchen:appliance`), espresso shots (`espresso:shot`), pantry inventory (`pantry:item`), kombucha brew (`kombucha:reading`).
app: ESP32/ESPHome kitchen sensors (sourdough rise, BBQ/sous-vide probes, fridge/freezer temperature), espresso-shot logs, and pantry inventory via MQTT and Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=kitchen:appliance appliance=oven
| stats latest(temp_c) as oven_temp, latest(target_c) as target
| eval ready=if(oven_temp>=target,"ready","still heating"), gap=round(target-oven_temp,0)
description: Tells you when the oven has genuinely reached the set temperature, which is often several minutes after the beep.
value: Ovens beep early and bake unevenly before they are truly hot; confirming real readiness improves everything you cook.
implementation: Ingest an oven temperature sensor; surface a simple ready or still-heating state against the target.
visualization: Single-value readiness indicator with the temperature gap to target.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Kitchen, Cooking & Fermentation — typical feeds: Sourdough monitor (`sourdough:reading`), BBQ/sous-vide probes (`bbq:probe`), fridge/freezer/oven temperature (`kitchen:appliance`), espresso shots (`espresso:shot`), pantry inventory (`pantry:item`), .
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `kitchen:appliance`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=kitchen:appliance`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** ESP32/ESPHome kitchen sensors (sourdough rise, BBQ/sous-vide probes, fridge/freezer temperature), espresso-shot logs, and pantry inventory via MQTT and Splunk HEC..

**Author notes:** Ingest an oven temperature sensor; surface a simple ready or still-heating state against the target.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "kitchen:appliance", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=kitchen:appliance earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Oven Preheat Readiness Confirmation** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=kitchen:appliance`) across the full search range. The `latest` aggregation groups by the time bucket; change the `by` clause if you want per-device, per-room, or per-user breakdowns instead.

**Fields this search depends on:** `ready`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=kitchen:appliance appliance=oven
| stats latest(temp_c) as oven_temp, latest(target_c) as target
| eval ready=if(oven_temp>=target,"ready","still heating"), gap=round(target-oven_temp,0)
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=kitchen:appliance earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table ready
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=kitchen:appliance earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.15.6: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Single-Value Readiness Indicator With The Temperature Gap To Target (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `kitchen:appliance` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=kitchen:appliance | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `aggregation` buckets.
